Precedent

PRESS-uh-dunt — starts like 'press'; a precedent gets pressed into use again and again by later cases. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Precedent is an earlier action, case, or decision that serves as an example or guide for later similar situations.

The court's landmark ruling set a precedent that lower courts would follow for decades.

Worked Example

A company allows one employee to work from home permanently after an injury. Soon, several other employees point to that decision and request the same arrangement for themselves.

The first employee's arrangement becomes the example others point back to — a precedent. Unlike 'rule,' which is written down and applies to everyone in advance, a precedent is a past case that people use afterward to justify similar treatment.

How Precedent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

example

example: a case used as a model for others

benchmark

benchmark: a standard used for comparison

model

model: a pattern others can follow

Antonyms

anomaly

anomaly: something that doesn't fit a pattern

exception

exception: a case that departs from the usual rule

How Strong Is It? — example → landmark → precedent

example vs. precedent

example vs. precedent: An example is weaker than a precedent — an example simply illustrates an idea, while a precedent is specifically used to guide and justify later decisions.

landmark vs. precedent

landmark vs. precedent: A landmark decision is stronger than a typical precedent: it isn't just an example others may follow, but a hugely influential case that reshapes how similar cases are handled from then on.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pre-

prefix — pre-: before (Latin)

root — -ced-

root — -ced-: to go, to yield (Latin)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: state of, noun-forming (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin cedere meant 'to go, to yield.' Something that has 'gone before' — praecedere — becomes a precedent, an earlier case that goes ahead of and guides the ones that follow.

Use the root in a new word: proceed

Use the root in a new word: proceed: Once the judge approved the motion, the lawyers were free to proceed with the trial.
